{{Recipe}}

'''Gurudi''', also called '''gurundi''', is a Nigerian coconut biscuit made from finely-grated coconut, cassava starch, and sugar.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]]
* 65 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] white [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 80 g [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|cassava starch]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]

== Procedure ==
# Gently crack open the coconut, and separate the meat from the shell. Use a [[Cookbook:Grater|grater]] or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] to shred the coconut.
# Combine the grated coconut, sugar, cassava starch, and nutmeg. Stir in water until it forms a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] ball.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] the dough until thin. Cut out square biscuits, and transfer them to a buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking tray]].
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the biscuits for about 20–25 minutes at 150°C (300°F) until golden brown and crisped.
# Remove the biscuits from the oven, and let cool.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* In the absence of cassava starch, [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]] or [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|corn starch]] can be used as a substitute.
* If desired, you can also use pre-shredded coconut.
